It is easy to get a bit lazy and up/downvoat submissions based merely on the title, without clicking on the link to affirm whether the content truly reflects the title. Sometimes the title has been manipulated by the submitter, and many times the title of the original submitted article was very misleading in the first place.

If a submission acquires enough upvoats, it will gain traction and may mislead even more people who tend to voat without clicking. Thus, a deceptive title will slowly sway public opinion in the wrong direction, and the inertia of that tendency can be difficult to overcome and reverse. This is one way disinformation and ignorance catches fire.

It is not too difficult to click and scope out the truth, but if you really do not want to click... it would be more responsible to not voat, either.

The choice is entirely yours, of course. I am merely stating my opinion on responsible voating.
In my opinion: It would be more responsible for us Voaters to click on links and discussion threads to investigate the validity of the claims in the title BEFORE making an up/downvoat.
